nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The census board covers a whole wall of the turbine hall. Names in chalk. Carly adds more every week.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The hospital ward runs on Galena heat. The library atrium is green: kale, potatoes, beans under lamps.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The council argues every night. Roz calls it democracy. Avila calls it a migraine. Both show up.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Over the door, someone painted Augie's words: SOMETHING TERRIBLE HAPPENED. WE DON'T KNOW WHAT. BE KIND.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Kessler runs the motor pool. He has one vote. He says it's the hardest posting he's ever had.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Every night the lamp line burns. Some nights something at the fence calls names. Nobody answers. Nobody knows how many. The lights stay on.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The list has 412 names. In December the valley had thirty thousand.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: It's honest now. Avila reads it aloud every Sunday, including the names she crossed off.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You keep the turbines. You have a warm bed and a pencil with an eraser. You use the eraser.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The turbines go east on hay sleds. Behind you, Galena goes cold, then the hospital.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: At Stillwater, the ground is warm and the Compact's greenhouses glow. Your father meets the first sled.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: From the canyon you watch Reno go dark, one window at a time. Something tall walks toward the last warm ones.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You crack the wellheads. Steam screams out of the ground for an hour, then fades.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Ruiz's charges are clean. Nobody is hurt. Nobody will ever kill for this place again.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You do it by hand, with a breaker bar and a sledge. It costs you. It's done.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The valley goes cold. The tall ones go still in the snow, sleeping. You walk south with everyone who trusts you.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You slip out before dawn with two packs and two coats. Nobody stops you. Nobody notices.

nodes.speaker: kit
nodes.text: [Radio static] ...Wrench? If you hear this, I'm going over Donner. Owe you three. Bye.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: And the Pearces—

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: [A letter on a feed receipt] Seed hay on the spring sled. Wes is bossing everybody. Come for lambing. — Dad

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: [A letter on a feed receipt] Hay on the spring sled. I'm proud of you. Should've said it first. — Dad

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: A letter comes in spring. One line on a feed receipt: 'Glad you're alive. — R.' You read it forty times.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Ross Pearce died in Fallon in the second winter. Wes brings the news in person. He stays.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: There's no one left to bring the news. You find out from a stranger on the road. You keep walking.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: And Carly—

nodes.speaker: carly
nodes.text: Address? Here. Breathing? Yes. Injuries? ...A few. Okay. Writing it down. So it happened.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Carly runs the Switchboard for her own people now. Some nights she radios. You always answer.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: And Wraith—

nodes.speaker: wraith
nodes.text: [Asleep against the warmest wall in the world, paws twitching, chasing something in a dream. Winning.]

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Her collar hangs on the hook by the door. Every kid who comes in asks about it. You tell them. Every time.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: ASHFALL
